key_insight: GeoABC uses boundary geometry to inject anisotropic, direction-aware corrections into neural operator features so models better capture near-wall aerodynamic physics.
engineering_relevance: This improves surrogate CFD accuracy where it matters most for design—near solid surfaces—helping predict pressure and flow behavior more reliably for airfoils and cars.
method: Condition boundary correction on geometry to distinguish tangential flow propagation from normal wall constraints.
Apply the correction inside intermediate neural operator representations rather than using geometry only as static input.
Works as a plug-in framework across multiple neural operator backbones.
evidence_signal: On 2D airfoil and 3D car benchmarks, GeoABC reduced near-boundary relative L2 error by about 38% on average.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on accurate boundary geometry and may add implementation complexity when integrating with different neural operator architectures.
paper_title: Geometry-Aware Anisotropic Boundary Correction for Aerodynamic Simulation
